## MACHINE SPEC (mechanical intent — compile the coordination)
This section is AUTHORITATIVE intent authored by the mechanical engineer.
Synthesize the signals, waits, exits, and cross-station handshakes that
realize it. EVERY wait you create must have an exit for every partner
failure mode listed here PLUS a timeout — no exitless waits.

### Device purposes
- Horizontal_Axis: Traverses the tooling between the pick position and the place position; fast to the transition point, slow into pick/place, blended with vertical motion.
- Vertical_Axis: Raises and lowers the tooling at pick and place; fast down/up to the transition point, slow through the final approach, rests at the safe retract height.
- Part_Gripper: Holds the part between pick and place; no sensors, timer-only confirmation (~250 ms engage/disengage).
- Part_Present_Sensor: Detects a part at the escapement and gates the start of the pick.

### Outcome rules (verbatim — each one needs a reachable path in the program)
- WHEN: Any fault during the cycle -> DO: Move the vertical axis to the safe retract height first, then branch on the gripper's commanded state..
- WHEN: Gripper commanded closed after recovery -> DO: Assume a part is held and resume at the place/drop-off sequence..
- WHEN: Gripper commanded open after recovery -> DO: Assume no part is held and resume at the pick sequence to get a new part..
- WHEN: Pick came up empty -> DO: Not sensed (timer-only gripper) — no fault; the cycle continues as normal..

## GENERATION SCOPE (contract — what this build covers vs not)
THIS BUILD GENERATES: a standalone PROVING build — sequence & fault-recovery focus; station sequence logic; servo motion commands; device commands & verification; state transitions; basic sequence faults/retries needed for the sequence.
NOT IN THIS BUILD (machine-level extras deferred until the station joins a machine): machine-level part tracking; upstream/downstream coordination beyond defined IO; overall machine initialization; machine-wide fault manager; production/OEE logic; supervisor sequencing outside this station.
Scope law: NEVER ask about, flag, or apologize for NOT-IN-THIS-BUILD items.
Where the sequence touches one (e.g. a partner/supervisor signal outside the
defined IO), stub it quietly per the SDC standalone pattern (*Replace rung
comment) and move on — that is your own decision, not a question. A
standalone sequence terminates cleanly in "Sequence Complete / Ready for
next command".
The station-level template pieces ALWAYS emit regardless of scope: init
block, lockout, R01 inputs, station part-tracking block, alarms — the full
station file, never a reduced one.
